div.head: IV Eg 1.7
div.ab: ⁊ þa Godes þeowas, þe þa sceattas underfoð, þe we Gode syllað, libban clænan life, þæt hy þurh þa clænnysse ús to Gode þingian mægen.
⁊ ða Godes þeowas, þe ða sceattas underfoð, þe we Gode syllað, libban clænan life, þæt hy ðurh ða clænnysse ús to Gode þingian mægen.

Sanctęque ęcclesię cultores, per quorum manus transeundum est quod Domino uniuersorum pro nostrarum salute animarum damus, inreprehensibiliter casteque et sancte uiuant, sicut decet Dei ministros, quatinus sua sanctitate pro nobis apud Altissimum mereantur fieri intercessores.
⁊ ða Godes þeowas þe ða sceattas underfoð, þe we Gode syllað, libban clænan life, þæt hy ðurh ða clænnysse ús to Gode þingian mægen;
Und die Geistlichen, welche jene Gelder empfangen, die wir Gott geben, sollen keusches Leben führen, damit sie vermöge dieser Keuschheit für uns zu Gott fürbittend eintreten können.
And the servants of God who receive the payments that we give to God are to live a chaste life, so that through that chastity they may intercede for us with God.
And that the servants of God who receive the dues which we render to Him shall live a pure life, so that, by virtue of their purity, they may intercede for us with God.
And those servants of God who receive the dues which we pay to God, are to live a pure life, that through that purity they may intercede for us to God.
div.note: BF: added from Gesetze I p. 208, October 2026 (MS C (Latin)); O: corrected against Gesetze I, October 2026 (was “(Latin version of C)”, now “∅ (moved to BF)”)

note.seg: Wiederum schmückt Versio den Stil und möchte das Kirchenvermögen vom Odium der Selbstsucht der Geistlichen reinigen
Once again the Versio embellishes the style and seeks to clear church property of the odium of clerical self-interest
Vgl. Gl Cölibat 1ff.; Geistliche 22. 26a. Kraft der Fürbitte (d. 1) hängt von Keuschheit ab; Hom. n. Wulfstan 120. 179. Das Interesse der Laien an ihr bekennen die Urkunden
Cf. Gl Cölibat 1ff.; Geistliche 22. 26a. The efficacy of intercession (d. 1) depends on chastity; Hom. n. Wulfstan 120. 179. The charters bear witness to the laity’s interest in it

During the reign of Edgar great efforts were made to restore monasticism and to oust secular priests and canons from collegiate churches and cathedrals. For the history of this movement see Hunt, The English Church from the Foundation to the Norman Conquest, pp. 326–68.
